title: GovTech and Google DeepMind developing real-time detection of AI scams on devices
key_facts: The Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech) is working with Google DeepMind on real-time detection of AI scams on devices, Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo said on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026.
The on-device AI model is meant for Android devices, Google said in a press release.
It analyses conversational patterns locally, without sending data to external servers, and shows a warning on screen when it detects a scam.
Google said it is fine-tuned on local scam narratives, including impersonations of public institutions, banks and local figures, and will keep training; installation details will be announced soon.
Teo said AI has made the fight against scams "harder to win" and that Singapore's response should be to "tune up our defences".
GovTech and the Singapore Police Force's system uses AI to scan more than 600,000 websites a day and disrupts around 20,000 malicious websites a month.
At the same event Teo announced a quantum-safe kickstarter grant (1 Nov 2026 to 31 Oct 2027) and said guidance for other organisations to migrate to quantum-safe encryption by 2035 will follow.
